sections.title: Basic Strategy for Sentence Improvement
sections.content: In Sentence Improvement questions, a part of the sentence is underlined and must be corrected according to proper grammar. Follow 2–3 steps to solve it: Step 1: Identify the Subject and Verb. Step 2: Check the Tense, Article, Preposition, and Pronoun. Step 3: Choose the option that forms the clearest and grammatically correct sentence.

sections.title: Basic Rules of Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the subject and check whether it is singular or plural. Step 2: Choose the verb according to the subject. Step 3: Use a singular verb with special words like Each, Everyone, Someone. Example: 'Each of the students are ready' is incorrect. Correct: 'Each of the students is ready.'

sections.title: Correct Use of Tense
sections.content: Step 1: Look for time indicators (since, for, yesterday, now). Step 2: Choose the correct tense accordingly. Step 3: Check whether continuous or perfect tense is required. Example: 'He is living here since 2010' is incorrect. Correct: 'He has been living here since 2010.'

sections.title: Basic Prepositions and Articles
sections.content: Step 1: Check whether an article (a, an, the) is needed before the noun. Step 2: Choose the correct preposition (in, on, at). Step 3: Verify the usage according to the meaning. Example: 'He is good in mathematics' is incorrect. Correct: 'He is good at mathematics.'

sections.title: Noun and Pronoun Case Correction
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the correct case of the pronoun (subject or object). Step 2: Choose the pronoun according to the verb. Step 3: Check the possessive form if needed. Example: 'Me and Ram went to market' is incorrect. Correct: 'Ram and I went to the market.'

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Using a plural verb with a singular subject. 2. Using incorrect tense with Since/For. 3. Omitting articles. 4. Incorrect use of prepositions. 5. Wrong pronoun case.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Sentence Improvement, first check Subject-Verb agreement, then verify tense and prepositions, and finally correct articles and pronouns. The simplest and clearest option is usually the correct one.

tricks.title: Subject-Verb Quick Check
tricks.explanation: First identify the subject and determine whether it is singular or plural.
tricks.example: Each of the players is ready.

tricks.title: Vowel Sound Article Rule
tricks.explanation: Use 'an' before a vowel sound and 'a' before a consonant sound.

tricks.title: Time Preposition Shortcut
tricks.explanation: In = month/year, On = day/date, At = exact time.

tricks.title: Pronoun Order Rule
tricks.explanation: Place 'I' at the end in a sentence when mentioning multiple subjects.
tricks.example: Ram and I went to the market.

tricks.title: Continuous vs Perfect Check
tricks.explanation: If Since/For appears, perfect continuous tense is often used.
tricks.example: He has been working here for 5 years.

tricks.title: Common Preposition Pair
tricks.example: Interested in, Good at, Afraid of.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Trick
tricks.explanation: Immediately eliminate options that break grammar rules.
tricks.example: If the subject is singular, remove options with plural verbs.
